Sources: comparative study by Software in a Box covering eight countries (Nov. 2026) · Regulation (EU) 2025/327

p01.loc: Dental data are the great absentees of the European Health Data Space. Not for lack of value, but because of how dentistry is organised. Across Europe, most practices are small businesses with their own software. In some countries public insurance pays for dental care; in others, families and private insurers pay almost everything. We studied eight countries and found two funding models, and none of them has yet formally designated its health data access body. In nearly all of them, clinical dental data stay in each practice, with no registry for adults and no link to national health records. The data exist, they are abundant, and their owners have reasons to share them under control. What is missing is someone to connect them. That is Dental Data.

Source: Dental Data · the solution and its use cases (public knowledge base)

That is how a federated data space works.
p02.loc: In a federated data space, each practice, chain, insurer or payer keeps its records in its own practice management software. A connector is installed next to that software. The connector publishes in a common catalogue which data exist, but not the data themselves. When someone needs an indicator, the question travels to each practice, is computed there, and only the aggregated result comes back. Consents, metadata and results move over the network. Never an identifiable record. The data stay in the practice. What travels is the answer.

p03.loc: Do the data leave the practice? No. No identifiable record leaves the practice. Every use of the data is governed by a digital contract that defines who accesses, for what and for how long. And that contract does not stay on paper: the machine enforces it itself. If a request has no contract, there is no access. If it has one, only an aggregated result comes back. The practice always decides, within the framework of the General Data Protection Regulation and national law in each country, under the supervision of its data protection authority. And with a clear rule of the European Health Data Space: health data are never used for advertising.

p04.loc: A dental chain grows by acquiring practices, and each practice comes with its own software. Across Europe, chains and groups are consolidating fast. Comparing quality today means migrating records, a costly and risky process. With Dental Data there is no need. A connector is installed next to each software, and the indicators are computed in each practice with the same definition, based on clinical guidelines. Management sees comparable results for the whole network, without a single record moving. And the chain can demonstrate its quality to regulators, payers and insurers, ready for the European Health Data Space. Demonstrable quality, without migrating a single record.

p05.loc: An insurer, a mutual or a public payer works with hundreds of practices, each with its own software, and cannot compare their results. Dental Data gives it consistent data from the whole network without centralising records: the computation happens in each practice and only the aggregated result comes back. The same applies to public dental programmes and reforms, which will have to measure their outcomes. With clear limits: the European Health Data Space prohibits using these data for advertising or for decisions that harm people, including in insurance. Consistent data from the whole network, without centralising records.

How does AI on dental X-rays work?

Sources: Dental Data (knowledge base) · Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 · Regulation (EU) 2025/327 · Model in clinical validation; it does not replace the professional's diagnosis · Supervision: national medical device authorities and AI Act authorities

AI on dental images without moving X-rays.
p06.loc: Training a dental AI requires many X-rays. But pooling them in one place is a risk. Dental Data reverses the path: the algorithm travels to each practice, learns there and returns only what it learned, never the images. The computations use confidential computing, which protects the data while they are being processed. The first model, for interproximal caries and periodontal bone loss, is in clinical validation. It is an aid for the professional: it does not replace their diagnosis. And it is getting ready for what comes next: in two thousand thirty-one, medical images enter the European Health Data Space. The algorithm goes to the data.

p07.loc: The European Health Data Space is already in force and has dates. By March two thousand twenty-seven, each country must designate its access bodies. In March two thousand twenty-nine, most of the rules on secondary use apply, and in two thousand thirty-one medical images arrive, such as dental X-rays. Most practices are micro-businesses and are exempt by default: to take part they need an aggregated channel, through chains, associations or insurers. Each Member State is preparing its access body: some have a draft law, others a candidate agency. None had been formally designated by November two thousand twenty-six. Whoever arrives connected will be the natural partner.

p08.loc: Dental Data follows a simple rule: Microsoft inside the node, open standards at the borders. Inside each node, the connector runs on Microsoft Azure, with the data in the European Union, integrated with the practice management software and deployed by Azure partners. At the borders, the space speaks open European standards: Gaia-X, the dataspace protocol, Eclipse EDC, verifiable credentials, FHIR, DICOM and HealthDCAT-AP. So any participant can connect, even without Microsoft. And we are not starting from scratch: Software in a Box has already designed and run three real data spaces. In France, the node is also available on a certified sovereign provider.

Manufacturers of implants and materials, and artificial intelligence companies, need to know how their products perform in the practice. p11.loc: This is what we build on Microsoft Azure for Dental Data. One rule guides the design: Microsoft inside the node, open standards at the border. In the practice, the X-ray leaves the unit through an open source DICOM gateway, Orthanc, and is pseudonymised at source. In the data node, Azure Health Data Services stores the record in FHIR and the image in DICOM. Microsoft Fabric and OneLake prepare the data for analysis. Security comes from Microsoft Entra ID, Azure Key Vault, Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Microsoft Sentinel. At the border, the Eclipse EDC connector works, deployed on Azure Kubernetes Service. It publishes the catalogue in HealthDCAT-AP, negotiates ODRL contracts and identifies itself with Gaia-X credentials. The artificial intelligence is trained with Azure Machine Learning and federated learning: the model travels to each practice and the data stay where they are. Confidential computing protects the data even during processing, and Microsoft Foundry writes draft reports that the dentist reviews. So every X-ray follows a safe and controlled path, from the practice to the model, without any identifiable data leaving the node.
